info.title: Kete API
info.description: Nutrition-aware meal planner. Record your measurements once, write your own recipes, arrange them into a week, and see the week's totals against your computed targets.

put.description:
Update the signed-in user's account details.

Changing the username or email needs current_password, because either one
is what the account signs in with (S14). Changing only the name does not.

401.description: Bearer token missing, malformed or expired

404.description: The account behind the token no longer exists

409.description: That username or email is already taken

delete.description:
Delete the account and everything in it, given the password.

The ORM deletes the children, not the database. Every relationship on
User is cascade="all, delete-orphan", so db.delete(user) loads the
profile, the target, the recipes and the plan slots and deletes each
before the user row goes. The schema's ON DELETE CASCADE stands behind it
for a delete made in SQL, but this path never reaches it. That is what
section 7.2 and ADR 010 describe, and this is the only caller.

Photographs are the exception. They live in S3, which no foreign key
reaches, so their keys are read first and each object is removed once the
rows are gone, best effort, as delete_recipe does for one. Deleting them
first would lose them if the commit then failed.

put.description:
Replace the password, given the current one.

Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire (twelve hours at most):
a token carries no record of the password it was issued under, and ending
them early would need a per-user counter in the schema. A known limitation,
recorded in the report, not an oversight.

get.description:
Read back the saved body metrics, so the form can prefill.

Separate from GET /profile on purpose: `profiles` is the most sensitive
table in the system, and the account screen has no use for it. These five
figures travel only when something asks for them by name.

401.description: Bearer token missing, malformed or expired

404.description: No measurements saved yet. A state, not a failure: the form offers an empty prefill.

post.description:
One request, two tables.

1. Save the raw body metrics into `profiles`.
2. Run the nutrition engine on them.
3. Save the computed result into `nutrition_targets`.

Both writes happen in a single transaction, so either both land or neither
does. That matters: stored targets must never disagree with the metrics
they came from.

get.description:
Read the computed targets.

Note this reads `nutrition_targets` only. It never touches `profiles`, so
the sensitive body metrics are not re-read every time a screen loads.

get.description:
Each day's planned totals against the daily targets (FR-16).

Seven entries, Mon to Sun. A day with nothing planned is still returned,
with zero totals: an empty day is a result, not a missing one. Each day's
total is the sum of its slots' per-serving figures exactly as GET /mealplan
shows them, so the grid and these totals always add up. The design is ADR
001.

post.description:
Fill a whole week from the user's recipe library.

Clears the week first, then deals recipes round-robin across all 21 slots,
so the same recipe does not land twice in a row while the library is small.

Choosing recipes to best hit the nutrition targets is future work; this
version just fills the week.

get.description:
Liveness only: is the process up and serving?

Deliberately does not touch the database. A health check that fails when
the database is unreachable is a readiness check, and behind a load
balancer it takes the instance out of service for a fault it cannot fix
by restarting. If a database probe is wanted, it belongs at its own path.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description:
The shape of every error this application raises.

FastAPI's own request validation answers 422 with `detail` as a list of
field errors instead, so a client cannot read the two the same way. The
rule is stated in section 3 of the implementation design.

total.title: Total
total.description: The day's planned total for this nutrient: the sum of its slots' per-serving figures, exactly as GET /mealplan reports them.

target.title: Target
target.description: The stored daily target for this nutrient.

difference.title: Difference
difference.description: total minus target. Negative is under target, positive is over.

percent.title: Percent
percent.description: total as a whole-number percentage of target, rounded half up, so 46.5 becomes 47. A stored target is never zero, so this is always a whole number.

NutrientComparison.title: NutrientComparison
NutrientComparison.description:
One nutrient on one day, against the stored daily target.

These four descriptions travel into openapi.json, for the reason the
declared error responses below give: a fact a client has to know is part
of the contract, and a comment here is not. The sign of `difference` and
the length of `days` were both comments until a cross-lane review pointed
out that C18's grid was being built on them.

photo_url.title: Photo Url
photo_url.description: A temporary link to the stored photograph. null when the photograph was stored but a link to it could not be signed just now; reading the recipe again gives a fresh one.

week.title: Week
week.description: ISO 8601 week, for example 2026-W39. The year is the ISO week-numbering year and not the calendar year: format it with %G-W%V, never %Y-W%V. JavaScript has no built-in for this. A week computed the wrong way is well-formed, passes this pattern and points at the wrong seven days, which shows up only in late December.

current_password.title: Current Password
current_password.description: Required when username or email changes, since either is what the account signs in with. Not needed to change only the name.

days.title: Days
days.description: Always seven entries, Mon to Sun, in that order. A day with nothing planned is present with zero totals, the full negative difference and 0 percent: an empty day is a result, not a missing one.
